CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
42-year-old female presents with a 5-day history of right index finger pain sustained while skiing double black diamond slopes last Saturday. Patient reports loss of control while skiing and flipped down the slope, jamming her index finger on an unknown object during the fall. Pain is rated 7 out of 10. She has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. No other injuries sustained during the fall. Has not iced or splinted the finger prior to this visit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No other injuries reported from the skiing incident. No other systemic complaints elicited.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation.
Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation.
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, taken for finger pain with minimal relief).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skier; recently engaged in double black diamond skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand examination: Normal x-ray of right hand with all joints and bones in appropriate alignment; no fractures identified. Right index finger: Tenderness elicited with palpation, traction, and compression over the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: No fractures; normal alignment of all bones and joints.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right index finger DIP joint sprain. Patient to be placed in a splint on right index finger. Prescribed Mobic 15 mg once daily for 14 days for anti-inflammatory effect. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine if hand therapy is needed. Patient to return for re-evaluation at that time.
